questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to choose a strong password
How banks protect their customers
Why social media is bad for teenagers
Why online fraud is so easy for criminals
questions.why: Neil says they'll find out why it's so easy for fraudsters to steal our money online.

questions.q: What kind of passwords do Neil and Georgina admit to using?
options: Long random numbers that they change every month
Strong passwords that a computer creates for them
Easy ones, like a mother's maiden name or first pet
A different password for every account they have
questions.why: Georgina uses things like her mother's maiden name, and Neil mentions the name of a first pet.

questions.q: Why do some people see online fraud as an attractive crime?
options: It makes a lot of money with fairly low risk
It is legal in many countries
It needs very expensive equipment
Victims usually get their money back
questions.why: Neil says it's regarded as a highly profitable and relatively low-risk crime.

questions.q: What do businesses pay Rachel Tobac to do?
options: Train their staff to write emails
Break into their systems to find weak spots
Catch fraudsters and take them to court
Design new banking software
questions.why: She is an 'ethical fraudster' whom businesses employ to hack their systems and find weak spots.

questions.q: According to Rachel, where can attackers find useful information about you?
options: Only from letters stolen from your post box
Mainly from your bank and credit card records
Only from official government records about you
From LinkedIn and your Instagram screenshots
questions.why: She says they find your assistant or accountant on LinkedIn and your emails from Instagram screenshots.

questions.q: What is an example of a fraudster's cover story?
options: Offering a free holiday
Pretending to call from your bank
Selling cheap computer software
Asking for help with a school project
questions.why: Neil says they may pretend to be calling from your bank or credit card company.

questions.q: What does Neil say about many victims of modern fraudsters?
options: They usually catch the criminals themselves
They lose only small amounts
They only notice after their bank accounts are empty
They are mostly large companies
questions.why: He says many victims only realise after their bank accounts have been emptied.

questions.q: What does Georgina decide to do at the end?
options: Change her passwords soon
Close her social media accounts
Stop shopping online
Call her bank
questions.why: She says she's going to change her passwords soon – 'Better safe than sorry!'
